rules.quote: Always write in plain language.
rules.specification: Assess vocabulary and sentence complexity against the intended recipient. The page supplies no numerical readability threshold.
rules.violation_condition: An email or letter uses language unnecessarily difficult for its intended recipient to understand.
when: The text is an email or letter.
rules.why: G-1: plain language is a distinct requirement under the combined language-and-tone heading.

covers.quote: Use the right level of formality for the recipient and purpose.
The level of formality in the writing depends on the recipient and the purpose.
When you write emails or letters for work, use the right format and tone for the purpose.

rules.quote: Consider the needs of the person who will get the email or letter and choose the right tone.
rules.specification: Assess tone against the recipient relationship and communicative purpose, rather than requiring formal language in all correspondence.
rules.violation_condition: The tone of an email or letter is inappropriate for its recipient, relationship or purpose.
when: The text is an email or letter.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the repeated requirement for recipient- and purpose-appropriate tone.

rules.quote: you must give them the option to unsubscribe.
rules.violation_condition: A mailing-list email gives its recipients no option to unsubscribe.
when: The email is sent through a mailing list.
rules.why: G-5: an unsubscribe option is a property of the message; obtaining permission to add someone is a separate operational obligation.

covers.quote: If you’re sending a letter to someone in an organisation, include:
the recipient’s position
the branch or division they work in
the name of the organisation.

rules.quote: Include the recipient’s name and postal address at the top of the letter.
rules.violation_condition: A letter lacks the recipient’s name or postal address at the top, or its address block omits the additional organisational details required for a recipient in an organisation.
when: The text is a letter.
For a recipient in an organisation, also include their position, branch or division, and organisation name.
rules.why: G-2: organisational recipients add conditions to one address-block completeness check.

covers.quote: Make sure the recipient’s details are correct.

rules.quote: Use information only if it is accurate, up to date, complete and relevant.
rules.specification: Apply this paragraph in its Address blocks context. Verification requires an authoritative current source for recipient details. Missing address components belong to the address-block completeness check, not a second finding here.
rules.violation_condition: A letter’s recipient or address details contain inaccurate, outdated or irrelevant information.
when: The information appears in a letter’s recipient or address details.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the accuracy restatement; distinguish incorrect supplied details from missing address components.

rules.quote: With emails, explain in the covering text that the email has a letter attached.
rules.violation_condition: An email carrying an attached letter does not mention the attached letter in its covering text.
when: A letter is attached to the email.
rules.why: G-5: this specifies required covering words, unlike the adjacent advice about transmission services.

covers.quote: Copy people into an email if they need the email for information only.

rules.quote: Include recipients in the ‘To’ field only if you need them to act on something in the email.
rules.specification: The checker needs recipient fields and enough context to establish who is expected to act. Do not infer that every recipient not explicitly named in a request is information-only.
rules.violation_condition: The email’s To field includes a recipient who is receiving the message for information only and is not expected to act.
when: Recipient fields are available for inspection.
rules.why: G-2: action recipients and information-only recipients are cases of the same recipient-role check.

covers.quote: Use the ‘CC’ field if people all know each other or can look up an email address with ease.

rules.quote: Use the ‘BCC’ field to send an email to a group of people who don’t know each other.
rules.specification: Recipient relationships require external information. Do not infer that people know each other merely because their addresses share a domain.
rules.violation_condition: An email exposes a copied group’s addresses instead of using BCC when the people do not know each other.
when: The email is being copied to a group.
CC is appropriate when everyone knows each other or can readily look up an email address.
Use BCC for a group of people who do not know each other.
rules.why: G-2: CC and BCC are conditional alternatives within one copied-recipient privacy check.

rules.quote: For images in emails and digital letters, use alt text.
rules.violation_condition: An image in an email or digital letter has no alternative text.
when: The text is an email or digital letter containing an image.
Image and alternative-text information is available for inspection.
rules.why: G-5: this requires a textual alternative, rather than prescribing a file format or delivery method.

rules.quote: Don't send images unless they're referred to and described in the text.
rules.violation_condition: An email or digital letter includes an image that is not referred to and described in the accompanying text.
when: The text is an email or digital letter containing an image.
rules.why: G-5: the instruction imposes an explicit requirement on the accompanying words.

covers.quote: Include dates in letters

rules.quote: Include the date you are sending the letter so that the recipient knows when you wrote it.
rules.violation_condition: A letter does not include its sending date.
when: The text is a letter.
rules.why: G-4: the body specifies which date the heading requires.

covers.quote: Be clear and concise with the subject line. It should sum up the purpose of the email.
Write the subject line as a heading that helps people know what is in the email and why they should read it.
It’s what the recipient will read first and must make the purpose of the letter very clear.
Keep it short but informative.
The body of an email should reflect the subject line.

rules.quote: Write a clear and concise subject line
rules.specification: Treat wording as unnecessarily long when it can be removed without losing information needed to identify the purpose. Do not impose a numerical length limit. Compare the subject with the body when assessing whether it represents the correspondence.
rules.violation_condition: An email subject line or letter subject fails to identify the correspondence’s purpose, misrepresents its body, or contains unnecessary wording.
when: The text is an email or letter with a subject.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate subject clarity, concision and correspondence with the body rather than flagging the same misleading subject twice.

rules.quote: As for all headings, it is good practice to put the main idea first.
rules.specification: Identify the main idea from the email’s purpose. Flag front-loaded secondary information, not a fixed number of introductory words.
rules.violation_condition: An email subject line places subsidiary wording before its main idea.
when: Assessing an email subject line.
rules.why: G-1: information order is independently checkable even when a subject is otherwise clear and concise.

rules.quote: Avoid using expressions and words that make the email look like spam or like a suspicious email.
rules.specification: The page supplies no expressions, lexicon or decision criteria. Agree contextual criteria before generating automatic findings.
rules.violation_condition: An email subject uses wording that makes the message look like spam or a suspicious email.
when: Assessing an email subject line.
rules.why: G-1: suspicious wording is a separate defect from subject length or information order.

covers.quote: Use ‘Dear’ in a more formal context and ‘Hi’ in a more informal context, such as emailing a colleague.

rules.quote: Stay on topic and write only what the recipient needs to know.

when: The text is an email or letter.
